info.title: LUXORA Platform API
info.description: Every route the platform serves. A store's systems call the admin routes with a store API key as a Bearer token (issued in Store console → AI → API & MCP keys; it acts with one staff role). Shopper routes use the shopper's session cookie. Platform routes need a platform administrator's session. Generated from the code — see docs/api/README.md.

session.name: azs
session.description: A shopper's or staff member's session; writes also send the azc cookie's value as the x-csrf header

get.description: ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── PLATFORM ADMIN ACCOUNTS — the console's own user base. The seed creates exactly one platform owner, and for the whole history of this build that was the *only* way to get a platform account: newPlatformAdmin() was called solely by the seed. So a second operator — a support admin, a second owner — had to be created by hand in SQLite, which is impossible in practice because the credentials are scrypt(v2) + peppered and the pepper context ("pa:" + email) is baked into the hash. This is the CRUD surface that fixes it. Platform-only, audited on the global hash-chained log, and it reuses the *same* primitives the seed and the login path use — newPlatformAdmin / hashPasswordFor / checkPassword — so a created account signs in at /platform.html with no second code path and no divergent hashing. ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

get.description: ---------- Global Platform: cross-tenant commerce data ---------- One generic reader serves every entity-backed store capability. The Store Console reads ONE tenant through /api/meta/entity/:key; the Platform Console reads ACROSS stores through /api/platform/data/:key. Both resolve through the same definitions, the same field whitelist and the same parameterized predicates in lib/entity.js, so a capability's data model is defined exactly once — the platform never forks a store's schema, and the store never diverges from the platform. GET /api/platform/data enumerates the served entities so the console builds its Global Operations surface from live metadata rather than a hardcoded menu (zero hard-coding).

post.description: A payment provider's webhook. The store's own gateway signing secret (Console → Payments, "Webhook signing secret") is tried first and confines the event to that store's payments; the platform's inbound secret is the fallback for a platform-operated account. How the signature is checked is the provider spec's `webhook.signature` (an HMAC over the body or URL + body, or the provider's own verify call); a spec that declares none uses the platform's scheme (`sha256=` / Stripe's `t=,v1=`). Only a verified event moves money state, and replays are no-ops.
